**Key Lemma:** For any prime *p* with gcd(10, *p*) = 1, if all 2017 column-codes and 2016 of the 2017 row-codes are divisible by *p*, then the remaining row-code is also divisible by *p*.

**Proof:** WLOG suppose row 1 is the supposedly non-divisible row, so $R_i \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$ for $i \geq 2$ and $C_j \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$ for all $j$.

From $C_j \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$:
$$a_{1j} \cdot 10^{2016} \equiv -\sum_{i=2}^{2017} a_{ij} \cdot 10^{2017-i} \pmod{p} \quad \forall\, j$$

Since $\gcd(10, p) = 1$, we can multiply by $10^{-2016}$:
$$a_{1j} \equiv -10^{-2016} \sum_{i=2}^{2017} a_{ij} \cdot 10^{2017-i} \pmod{p} \quad \forall\, j$$

Now compute $R_1$:
$$R_1 = \sum_{j=1}^{2017} a_{1j} \cdot 10^{2017-j} \equiv -10^{-2016} \sum_{j=1}^{2017} \sum_{i=2}^{2017} a_{ij} \cdot 10^{2017-i} \cdot 10^{2017-j} \pmod{p}$$

Rearranging the double sum:
$$= -10^{-2016} \sum_{i=2}^{2017} 10^{2017-i} \underbrace{\sum_{j=1}^{2017} a_{ij} \cdot 10^{2017-j}}_{= R_i \equiv 0} \equiv 0 \pmod{p}$$

This contradicts $R_1 \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$. By symmetry (transposition), the same holds if the non-divisible code is a column. **Therefore no prime $p \neq 2, 5$ can work.**

## p = 2 works

Divisibility by 2 depends only on the last digit. Set:
- Last row: $a_{2017,j} = 2$ for all $j$ (all even)
- Last column: $a_{1,2017} = 1$ (odd), $a_{i,2017} = 2$ for $i \geq 2$ (even)

**Divisibility check:** Row 1 has last digit 1 (odd → not divisible by 2). All other rows have last digit 2 (even). All columns have last digit 2 (even). Exactly one non-divisible code. ✓

Row $i$ vs column $j$: if $i = j$, the row has 3 at position $i-1$ while the column has 3 at position $j+1$ — different positions, so different codes. If $i \neq j$, the 2s are at different positions. Row 2017 = 222...2 and column 2017 = 122...2 are distinct from each other and from all other codes (which contain 1s in most positions). All 4034 codes are distinct. ✓

## p = 5 works

Divisibility by 5 (with digits 1–9) requires last digit 5. Use the same interior, but set:
- Last row: $a_{2017,j} = 5$ for all $j$
- Last column: $a_{1,2017} = 1$, $a_{i,2017} = 5$ for $i \geq 2$

**Divisibility check:** Row 1 has last digit 1 (not 5 → not divisible by 5). All other codes have last digit 5 (divisible by 5). Exactly one non-divisible code. ✓

**Distinctness check:** Same structural argument — the interior pattern (1s with 2 on diagonal, 3 on subdiagonal) ensures all codes are distinct, and the last row (555...5) and last column (155...5) are distinct from each other and from all other codes. ✓
